prompt.es: Discute la encuesta vecinal: método, dos resultados, un límite y una propuesta.

answer.text: Last June a survey was conducted among three hundred residents of the old neighbourhood. The participants were selected at random from a list and were asked to complete a questionnaire online. Two results stand out. First, roughly a third of the residents said that the street lighting is poor. Second, twice as many older residents as young ones feel unsafe at night. These findings suggest that lighting may be a priority for the neighbourhood, and they appear to show that older people are more worried. However, there is an important limitation: most answers came from two streets, and the residents described their own feelings, so the data may be biased. For that reason, we cannot generalise the results to the whole city. As a next step, we propose a three-month trial of new lamps in the two streets, and we suggest that the council should report the results in the autumn. Further research with a larger sample would then show whether the change really helped.
accepted: Last June a survey was conducted among three hundred residents of the old neighbourhood. The participants were selected at random from a list and were asked to complete a questionnaire online. Two results stand out. First, roughly a third of the residents said that the street lighting is poor. Second, twice as many older residents as young ones feel unsafe at night. These findings suggest that lighting may be a priority for the neighbourhood, and they appear to show that older people are more worried. However, there is an important limitation: most answers came from two streets, and the residents described their own feelings, so the data may be biased. For that reason, we cannot generalise the results to the whole city. As a next step, we propose a three-month trial of new lamps in the two streets, and we suggest that the council should report the results in the autumn. Further research with a larger sample would then show whether the change really helped.

We conducted a survey in June, and three hundred residents of the old town answered an online questionnaire. They were chosen at random from a local list. We found two main things. To begin with, about a third of the residents think the street lighting is bad. In addition, double the number of older people compared with young people feel unsafe when they walk at night. This indicates that better lighting could be a priority, and it seems that older residents are more concerned. Nevertheless, there is a limitation. Most of the answers came from two streets, and people only reported how they feel, so the results may not be reliable. We therefore cannot say that the same is true for the whole city. Our proposal is a trial of three months with new lamps in those streets, and we recommend that the council reports the results in the autumn. More research with a larger sample would show whether the trial helped.

origin.text: Encuesta vecinal (junio): 300 residentes del barrio antiguo, elegidos al azar de una lista, respondieron un cuestionario en línea. Resultados: un tercio (34 %) dice que el alumbrado es malo; el doble de mayores que de jóvenes se siente inseguro por la noche. Límite: respondieron sobre todo vecinos de dos calles y los datos son declarados. Propuesta: una prueba de tres meses con farolas nuevas y un informe del ayuntamiento. Escribe entre 160 y 300 palabras en inglés.
